narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story; reads all narration and genealogies.

joseph-the-patriarch.name: Joseph
joseph-the-patriarch.note: Jacob's favoured son; candid dreamer at seventeen, then upright slave and calm interpreter of dreams in prison.

potiphars-wife.name: Putiphar's wife
potiphars-wife.note: Joseph's mistress; seductive and insistent, then falsely accusing with feigned outrage.

1.t: And Joseph was brought into Egypt, and Putiphar, an eunuch of Pharao, chief captain of the army, an Egyptian, bought him of the Ismaelites, by whom he was brought.

2.t: And the Lord was with him, and he was a prosperous man in all things: and he dwelt in his master's house:

3.t: Who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and made all that he did to prosper in his hand.

4.t: And Joseph found favour in the sight of his master, and ministered to him: and being set over all by him, he governed the house committed to him, and all things that were delivered to him:

5.t: And the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake, and multiplied all his substance, both at home and in the fields.

6.t: Neither knew he any other thing, but the bread which he ate. And Joseph was of a beautiful countenance, and comely to behold.

7.t: And after many days, his mistress cast her eyes on Joseph, and said:

8.t: But he in no wise consenting to that wicked act said to her:
Behold, my master hath delivered all things to me, and knoweth not what he hath in his own house:

9.t: Neither is there any thing which is not in my power, or that he hath not delivered to me, but thee, who art his wife; how then can I do this wicked thing, and sin against my God?

10.t: With such words as these day by day, both the woman was importunate with the young man, and he refused the adultery.

11.t: Now it happened on a certain day, that Joseph went into the house, and was doing some business, without any man with him:

12.t: And she catching the skirt of his garment, said:
But he leaving the garment in her hand, fled, and went out.

13.t: And when the woman saw the garment in her hands, and herself disregarded,

14.t: She called to her the men of her house, and said to them:
See, he hath brought in a Hebrew, to abuse us: he came in to me, to lie with me; and when I cried out,

15.t: And he heard my voice, he left the garment that I held, and got him out.

16.t: For a proof therefore of her fidelity, she kept the garment, and shewed it to her husband when he returned home:

17.t: The Hebrew servant, whom thou hast brought, came to me to abuse me.

18.t: And when he heard me cry, he left the garment which I held, and fled out.

19.t: His master hearing these things, and giving too much credit to his wife's words, was very angry,

20.t: And cast Joseph into the prison, where the king's prisoners were kept, and he was there shut up.

21.t: But the Lord was with Joseph, and having mercy upon him gave him favour in the sight of the chief keeper of the prison:

22.t: Who delivered into his hand all the prisoners that were kept in custody: and whatsoever was done, was under him.

23.t: Neither did he himself know any thing, having committed all things to him: for the Lord was with him, and made all that he did to prosper.
